newsitem.title: FINLAND: Rautaruukki well positioned for float - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Rautaruukki well positioned for float - CEO.

text.p: Finnish state-controlled steel group Rautaruukki Oy said on Thursday no decisions had been made on a potential further privatisation, but the group was well positioned for such a move despite lower 1996 earnings.

"Even though our earnings fell last year, the fall was not significant compared with many other companies in the sector," Rautaruukki CEO Mikko Kivimaki told a news conference when asked whether the 1996 report had provided conditions for a float.
Rautaruukki's profit before extraordinary items and tax was 715 million markka, down from 954 million in 1995.

"The market prospects are mostly favourable," Kivimaki said, adding that Rautaruukki's output capacity, hit by furnace repairs in 1995 and 1996, would increase in 1997 and this would also help earnings.
"If I were an investor, I would consider these facts," he said.
The ministry of trade and industry said in January it had appointed SBC Warburg and Union Bank of Switzerland as its advisers regarding a potential further privatisation of Rautaruukki.
The Finnish state holds 68.7 percent of shares in Rautaruukki, and has an authorisation by parliament to cut the state's ownership to 33.4 percent.
